the polarity conventions used in optics model, control system and magnet powering are consistent and the LHC optics model is correct.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the following topics: - the verification of the magnetic model for the LHC main dipoles and quadrupoles; - the investigation of higher order multipoles in the LHC quadrupoles and the verification of the corresponding optics model; - the verification of magnetic models for the LHC sextupole families; - the study of higher order multipole families in the LHC; - the study and verification of magnetic models and optics model for correctors in the LHC.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the magnetic model of the LHC is very accurate and the magnet circuits are well-understood.
the LHC magnetic field model is in very good agreement with the measured field distributions and the LHC optics models can therefore be used with confidence in the LHC operation.
the LHC magnetic field model is now in a very good agreement with the measurements, with the only exception of the sextupole family, where the model needs to be updated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the LHC optics model is well understood and that the magnet circuit assignments are correct.
the LHC optics model and the LHC magnet control system have been verified to work as intended.
the single-pass beam-based measurements of the LHC magnet circuit strengths are in good agreement with the optics models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
single-pass measurements of beam trajectories can be used as a powerful tool to validate the LHC magnetic models.
the LHC magnet model can be used to predict the effect of the magnetic circuits on particle trajectories with a precision better than 10 microns.
the LHC magnets can be accurately described by a model that is sufficiently detailed to allow the precise prediction of beam optics.
